inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. Organised by hundreds of groups, including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, the Together Alliance event was billed as the biggest [...] The post Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise appeared first on Digital Journal .
inputs.modified_text: This wasn’t a spontaneous public reaction: hundreds of groups, including unions and Muslim representative bodies, were involved, and the rally took place just weeks before local elections. The timing looks deliberate. Six months after one of Britain’s largest-ever far-right demonstrations, the same threat is being kept in the spotlight to steer political discussion and shape voters before they reach the polls. Although it is officially framed as a simple stand against extremism, mass rallies can also signal which views are acceptable and channel public opinion. I’d be wary of calling this organic.
